A lot of reviews have this game as having a royal amount of bugs. To be honest I haven't seen to many bugs (except when I'm running a ridiculous amount of mods or have a 600x600 prison.) Some of the bugs can be quite annoying though and game ruining. Like in gangs I found one where when you kick a gang out it'll still say they own it causing you to never be able to use that room or demolish. Or inmates not doing laundry in one of my prisons or the game occasionally pausing for a minute or two due to the prison being so big. As long as you're NOT using to many mods or making the prison absolutely gigantic (maybe it's cause I'm on a really bad laptop.) you should be fine. Gameplay wise this game is fun and you should play it. Watching a riot instantly disappear because you sent two armed guards who blast a guy away will never not be funny.

I bought PA originally through the crowdfunder back in 2012. It was a fantastic game, Introversion was fabulous at communicating throughout the Alpha and Beta testing and the released product was magnificent.

I am not particularly a game player, but I racked up almost 300 hours on this once it had been released onto Steam.

I was rather disappointed that the Introversion lads sold it off to Paradox, having seen what Paradox have done to other pieces of software that I used. The introduction of the 'launcher' was no real surprise, that comes along as baggage with all Paradox offerings, but the incessant tweaking to eventually hobble the game is a crying shame.

The whole point was that the community could work together to creatively make add-ons that would improve gameplay, but Introversions careful curation of that interface has been broken further and further to the stage that no-one really enjoys making add-ons any more. Had they at least left that alone, there would have been a ready community to keep the software alive well into the future: now Paradox are hauling along yet another dead duck.

Wind back time and run the 2018 version if you can, it's far superior.

A lot of games in the (city) building genre tend to all have a similar theme - while Cities:Skylines and Planetbase are fundamentally different in terms of gameplay they still offer very similar objectives - building a systainable city/colony where everything works.
I know Planetbase is not the best example for this, it does convey my point tho.

Here is where Prison Architect enters the field: It offers a completely new take on building something. Rather than managing big-scale cities and traffic you manage a Prison with all it's contents - cells, cell quality, laundry, cleaning, health.
The game starts small, as many others, but you can rapidly expand and create huge Prisons.
It is one of those games where you inevetably need to take multiple tries before finally getting it right as you usually run into problems. It is entirely possible to build a decent prison first try, but to get it running better you will need more tries and experience.

The game has a great pacing, you can begin expansion shortly after getting your first prisoner intake, but at the same time too rapid expansion is effectively limited by staff count and money.
Overall I can recommend this game as it is good fun and really enjoyable because it offers a unique concept and implementation.

> Build a functioning prison
> Get 5 legendary prisoners
> Build them their own prison on an island
> They start a small fight with normal guards
> They kill all 60 guards in their prison
> They find the armoury
> Call in a riot helicopter
> Prisoners shoot all riot guards until there's nothing left
> Seal off their prison
> Regret having those 5 legendary prisoners in the same 20 mile radius
> Download a toxic gas mod
> Gas the prisoners
> Prisoners survive
> Download army staff mod
> They shoot and kill all 40 heavily armed military units
> Stop worrying about that prison and wait for them to starve
> The prisoners die from starvation after 50 days of their non stop riot

I used to adore this game. However, that is not to say it didn't have its fair share of problems. These problems were only further exaggerated when the original developers sold the rights to the game over to Paradox Interactive. It has since been flooded with DLC, bugs, and enough lack-of-polish to be mistaken for corroded metal.

The user interface is a cluttered mess. The simulation is constantly suffering from problems such as kitchens not properly delivering food. Prisoners are left to rot because a cell of particular quality is not available. The graphics of the game are a mess, and there is a distinct lack of care when there is a tile that is literally a diagonal transition between grass and concrete rather than supporting transitions in the engine itself.

That is just to name a few, and I cannot stress enough how frustrating it is to watch the game's price skyrocket with downloadable content that might as well be a mod from the workshop. Can't wait for Prison Architect to cost hundreds of dollars like every other Paradox title.
